newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks edge to record high at open.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks edge to record high at open.

text.p: The Australian stock market scrambled to a record high at the open on Wednesday as local traders took their lead from stronger overseas markets.
The All Ordinaries index edged up 1.6 points to 2,630.5, touching a record high of 2,635.7 which surpassed the previous high of 2631.3 reached on Tuesday.
Brokers said today's steady start reflected the consolidative tone seen for most of last week.
"We have been looking for a pullback and yesterday could well have been the blow off the top," said a senior dealer at a Brisbane-based brokerage firm.

Banks, the popular sector of recent weeks, firmed early before profit-takers moved in. ANZ went to within a whisker of its record high, topping out at A$9.40 (US$7.14) before easing back to be 5.8 cents lower at A$9.28.

Commonwealth Bank suffered a similar fate, adding a few cents early before sellers slashed its shares to see it 15 cents lower at A$14.35. National Australia Bank, and Tuesday's sprinter Westpac Banking Corp, both added one cent to A$18.99 and A$7.47 respectively.
One positive in a patchy metals market was giant miner Rio Tinto, whose Australian shares followed their London sibling higher. Shares in Rio Tinto, formerly known as CRA, were up 32 at A$21.50.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about nine to five, while about 44 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
